candidates.change_summary: Change the return value from `true` to `false`.
Replace `uint _value = v * 10 ** _decimals;` with `uint _value = v;` so the transferred amount no longer scales by decimals, changing the call data.
Delete the `require(_tos.length > 0);` statement so the function no longer reverts on empty `_tos`, completing successfully with no external calls.

Replace `bytes4 id = bytes4(keccak256("transferFrom(address,address,uint256)"));` with `bytes4 id = bytes4(keccak256("transfer(address,uint256)"));` so a different function selector is called on `caddress`, changing external behavior.
Replace `for(uint i = 0;i < _tos.length;i++)` with `for(uint i = 0;i < _tos.length - 1;i++)` to skip the last recipient, changing external calls made.

Replace `caddress.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(id, from, _tos[i], _value))` with `caddress.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(id, from, _tos[0], _value))` so every iteration sends to the first recipient instead of the current one.

Replace `{ (bool _s, bytes memory _d) = caddress.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(id, from, _tos[i], _value)); _d; if (! _s) { revert();} }` with `{ (bool _s, bytes memory _d) = caddress.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(id, from, _tos[i], _value)); _d; }` to ignore call failures, allowing execution to continue instead of reverting.
Replace `uint _value = v * 10 ** _decimals;` with `uint _value = v * _decimals;` to use a different, non-standard scaling factor, altering the transferred amount.
Replace `_tos[i]` with `_tos[_tos.length - 1 - i]` in the call encoding to reverse the order of recipients.
